purpose: Source-reviewed election notices rendered as static briefs and RSS. Inbound feeds are review signals, not publishing inputs.

en.headline: Cabo Verde court admits sixth presidential bid
en.summary: CNE says a 24 September court appeal ruling admitted Loisito Tavares de Sousa, bringing the 15 November presidential field to six.
paragraphs: Cabo Verde's National Electoral Commission reported on 27 September 2026 that the Constitutional Court, in ruling 80/2026 dated 24 September, upheld an appeal by Loisito Tavares de Sousa and ordered his presidential candidacy admitted.

The CNE says this brings the number of admitted candidacies for the 15 November presidential election to six. Its notice names Gilson João dos Santos Alves, Joana Gomes Rosa Amado, José Maria Pereira Neves, Antero Lúcio Lopes Francês Tavares, Casimiro Jesus Lopes de Pina, and Loisito Tavares de Sousa. These are admitted candidacies reported by the CNE, not a final ballot order.

The commission's earlier 22 September notice described five admitted candidacies and an appeal window. The 27 September notice updates that count after one appeal ruling. Readers should check the CNE for any later court or ballot notices. An admissibility ruling is not an election result.

en.headline: Cabo Verde's initial court decision admitted five candidacies before appeal
en.summary: The CNE's 22 September notice described five candidacies admitted by the initial decision. A 27 September notice reports that an appeal brought the admitted count to six; this brief preserves the earlier decision.
paragraphs: Cabo Verde's National Electoral Commission reported on 22 September 2026 that the Constitutional Court had ruled on the admissibility of candidacies for the presidential election scheduled for 15 November. The court's order was dated 21 September.

According to the commission's notice, five candidacies were admitted, five were rejected, and one withdrawal was accepted. The notice says rejected applicants had 24 hours from notification to appeal to the full Constitutional Court.

This brief records the initial decision. In a 27 September notice, the CNE reported that the court admitted Loisito Tavares de Sousa after an appeal, bringing the admitted count to six. Neither notice is an election result or proof of a final ballot order.

en.headline: South Africa: Special-vote applications close 12 Oct
en.summary: The Electoral Commission says applications opened on 21 September for special votes ahead of the 4 November local elections. The deadline is 17:00 on 12 October.
paragraphs: South Africa's Electoral Commission said on 21 September 2026 that applications had opened for special votes in the local-government elections scheduled for 4 November. Its notice sets the application deadline at 17:00 on Monday, 12 October 2026.

The IEC describes two routes: an approved home visit for a voter unable to get to a voting station because of a physical condition, and an early visit to the registered voting station for a voter who cannot vote there on election day. The notice says approved station votes take place on the two days before 4 November.

The commission directs eligible voters to its website or a local IEC office to apply. It says the SMS route is only for a special vote at a voting station. Readers should use the IEC's official service to confirm eligibility, application status and any later timetable change; AfroTools is not the application portal.
